title: THE DESK — nestGate is the computer. TR-49 is the archetype. Rebuild the entire HUD as the in-game terminal.
kevin_declaration: THAT IS WHERE NESTGATE.IO DESK GOES? THAT IS THE INTERFACE? LIKE A CLASSIC MAC? LET REBUILD THE ENTIRE HUD AS THE COMPUTER AND SYSTEM IN THE GAME IN MY STEAM LIBRARY — TR-49. We archetype desks and computers and keyboards and then TR-49 Steam game is the HUD computer I want.

tr49_as_archetype.developer: inkle Ltd (Heaven's Vault, 80 Days, Overboard!, A Highland Song)
tr49_as_archetype.what_it_is: A WWII-era archive computer in a church basement. You enter 4-character codes (2 letters + 2 numbers) into a split-flap display. Each code reveals a book, letter, or journal from an interconnected archive of obscure texts. A voice guide (Liam) speaks through a crackling speaker. You deduce links between sources. You map the archive. You find the book that will rewrite the world.

the_interface.display: Sepia-toned circular tube display on the left — shows the current text/entry
the_interface.input: Split-flap mechanical display on the right — 4 characters (LL-NN format)
the_interface.audio: Crackling speaker — voice of handler/guide, responds to your exploration
the_interface.interaction: Enter codes → reveal texts → read → find clues → enter new codes → deeper
the_interface.aesthetic: Steampunk + WWII Bletchley Park. Tubes, wires, warm glow, mechanical clicks
the_interface.feeling: You are alone in a basement with a machine. The machine contains EVERYTHING. You just have to find the right codes.

why_perfect_for_hud.archive_of_texts: Our data/ folder IS the archive — 50+ JSON files, stories, plans, papers, game analyses
why_perfect_for_hud.code_system: Our file identifiers ARE the codes — wave numbers, spring names, primal names
why_perfect_for_hud.linking_sources: Our provenance trio (rhizoCrypt + loamSpine + sweetGrass) IS the link deduction
why_perfect_for_hud.voice_guide: Chipmunk IS Liam — narrates, guides, responds to exploration
why_perfect_for_hud.church_basement: nestGate IS the church basement — same location as origin (MSU), hidden, underground
why_perfect_for_hud.crack_the_code: Kevin IS cracking the code of reality — that's literally what ecoPrimals does
why_perfect_for_hud.machine_kept_working: The organism keeps running when Kevin sleeps (STALKER A-Life, cron jobs)
why_perfect_for_hud.the_machine_IS_the_interface: The HUD IS the organism looking at itself. The computer IS the only interaction.

desk_archetype_study.what_kevin_means: Before building, we study how 'computers inside games' work as a design pattern. The desk IS a game mechanic.

synthesis.the_pattern: In-game computers share a formula: CONSTRAINED INPUT + VAST ARCHIVE + DEDUCTION LOOP
synthesis.constrained_input: You can only type codes (TR-49), keywords (Her Story), or commands (Hacknet). The constraint IS the game.
synthesis.vast_archive: Behind the input is an enormous graph of interconnected content. You can only see one node at a time.
synthesis.deduction_loop: Read → notice clue → form hypothesis → input new query → read → deeper. The loop IS the gameplay.

our_version.input: Code entry (spring codes, wave numbers, primal names, file identifiers) + command bar (already exists in engine.html!)
our_version.archive: 50+ data files, stories, plans, papers, game analyses, visitor data, spring coordinates, all interconnected
our_version.deduction: Every file references other files. Every spring connects to other springs. Every primal connects to every other.
our_version.voice: Chipmunk narrates. Gaia responds. The organism speaks BACK to you.

nestgate_as_desk.what: nestGate.io IS the desktop. The computer surface. The place where the screen lives.
nestgate_as_desk.why: nestGate = content-addressed storage. The desk IS the filing cabinet. The computer IS the archive. Same location as origin (MSU). You don't travel to use it. It's RIGHT HERE in the basement.

aesthetic.base: TR-49's WWII archive terminal + Obra Dinn's 1-bit Mac + Kenshi's OS-as-game
aesthetic.display: Sepia/amber tube glow on dark background (already close to what we have!)
aesthetic.typography: JetBrains Mono (already have this!) — the typewriter/terminal font
aesthetic.colors: Amber (#d29922) primary, green (#3fb950) for live data, dim (#6e7681) for inactive
aesthetic.sounds: Mechanical clicks (split-flap), CRT hum, crackling speaker voice
aesthetic.chrome: Minimal — dark beveled frame, subtle scan lines, warm tube glow

layout.left: ARCHIVE DISPLAY — the sepia tube. Shows current text/entry. Like TR-49's main display.
layout.right: CODE INPUT — the split-flap. Where you enter identifiers to navigate the archive.
layout.bottom: STATUS BAR — already exists! wave, entities, beacons, selectivity, boundary
layout.top: HEADER — minimal. Machine name, connection status, voice indicator
layout.center: THE MAP — when zoomed out, shows the organism (current body map) or the earth (springs map)
layout.overlay: VOICE — chipmunk text appears as subtitle overlay, like TR-49's crackling speaker

code_system.what: Every piece of content in the organism gets a code. Like TR-49's LL-NN format.
code_system.navigation: Type a code → see the entry. Read it → find references to other codes → type those → spiral deeper. Exactly like TR-49.

build_plan.phase_1_desk_surface: Restyle nestGate.io as the TR-49 computer terminal. Dark background, amber tube glow, split-flap code input, mechanical aesthetic. The STATUS BAR (already working!) stays as the machine's instrument panel.
build_plan.phase_2_archive_wiring: Connect all 50+ data files as navigable archive entries. Each gets a SS-NNN code. Typing a code reveals the entry.
build_plan.phase_3_voice_layer: Wire chipmunk as the voice guide. Text subtitles overlay the bottom of the display. Chipmunk responds to what you're reading.
build_plan.phase_4_deduction_links: Highlight cross-references between entries. When you read about ludoSpring and it mentions 'wave function collapse', the code LS-042 appears as a clickable/typeable link.
build_plan.phase_5_map_integration: Zooming out from any entry shows its spring location on the Earth map. The code system IS the GPS. You are navigating both an archive AND a continent.
